newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end higher, PGMs jump.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end higher, PGMs jump.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended higher across the board on Friday, with platinum group metals (PGMs) extending their early gains to end mostly at their daily price limit highs, traders said.
The dollar's further rise against the yen prompted private investors to cover their shorts, they said.
All palladium futures hit fresh contract-highs.
All palladium futures except August, which has no daily price limit, closed up by their 36 yen per gram daily limits.
Benchmark June settled at 683 yen. Benchmark June platinum surged by its limit of 50 yen at 1,494 yen.
"Private investors, facing heavy losses, now realize they made a mistake," a trading house trader said.
They had built heavy shorts in PGMs based on an assumption that PGM prices would tumble after Russia resumed PGM exports.
But backed by lower-than-expected Russian spot sales and a tight physical market, traders expect the bullish trends to continue for most of this year, they said.

A strike in South Africa was also seen as supportive even though it was not a surprise. Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd said on Thursday the National Union of mineworkers had issued formal notification of a strike at its refineries from August 1.
Gold futures ended slightly higher, but static bullion prices limited price gains, while stronger dollar-based silver prices lifted silver futures, the traders said.
Gold futures ranged from two yen to 11 yen per gram up. Benchmark June was up seven yen at 1,229 yen. Benchmark June silver was up 5.7 yen per 10 grams at 174.0 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $325.00/50 per ounce at 0747 GMT, against $324.30/80 in New York on Thursday.
Activity in gold was lacklustre due partly to slower gold demand in the summer seasons.
